newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mt Edon says gold output above budget.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mt Edon says gold output above budget.

text.p: Mount Edon Gold Mines (Aust) Ltd said on Tuesday that Gold production from its Tarmoola and Nevoria mines in Western Australia were above expectations.
Gold production of 44,366 ounces for the five months to November 30 at Tarmoola ran about 2,100 ounces above budget, the company said.

At Nevoria, where mining ceased last week, improved operating practices and a successful salvage operation from the pit floor is expected to push gold producion to 26,000 ounces in 1996/97 (July-June) versus a budgeted 16,000 ounces, Mount Edon said.
Ore processing at Nevoria is expected to cease during April 1997, the company said.
The increased output will have a marked impact on cash flow at the company, where forward sales prices of A$650 per ounce covering 110,000 ounces, Mount Edon said.
Mount Edon also said it has awarded a three-year mining contract to mining services group MacMahon Holdings Ltd at Tarmoola, starting in January.
As part of the contract, MacMahon will acquire the mining fleet from Mount Edon, removing about A$13.2 million of lease and hire purchase debt from Mount Edon's balance sheet, it said.
A profit of some A$600,000 will be recorded on the sale of the fleet, it said.
On Monday, fellow Western Australia miner Westgold Resources said it had acquired a 6.75 precent stake in Mount Edon, attracted by Mount Edon's production assets and propsective properties.

However, Westgold managing director Mladen Ninkov, who wouldn't rule out making a bid for Mount Edon, told Reuters he thought Mount Edon's debts of around A$30 million was too high, which was weighing on the share price.
At 3.40 p.m. (0340 GMT), Mount Edon shares were trading at A$1.62, up two cents on the day but less than half its high for the year of A$3.50 a share.
